recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Which party governs which State/UT: In maps - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** and its allies secured victories in Assam, Puducherry, and West Bengal, while the Congress-led UDF won in Tamil Nadu. **Suvendu Adhikari**, a BJP leader, is set to become the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal. The results mark a shift in the political landscape with the BJP or the NDA now governing 20 states and 2 Union Territories.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Bangladesh seeks China support for Teesta restoration project - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bangladesh**’s new government has sought **China's** involvement in the Teesta River restoration project, a move that could strain relations with **India**.  The **Bangladesh** government is seeking to increase its share of the river's water under the 2011 Teesta water-sharing treaty, which has been blocked by **West Bengal**’s outgoing Chief Minister, **Mamata Banerjee**.  **China's** Foreign Minister, **Wang Yi**, pledged support for **Bangladesh's** new government and its development goals.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: Nepal lodges protest against India over long-running border dispute | Border Disputes News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nepal**'s Ministry of Foreign Affairs lodged a protest against **India** after the country announced the resumption of a religious pilgrimage through the Lipulekh Pass, which is claimed by **Nepal** based on a 1816 treaty.  **India** maintains that the pass has been used for pilgrimages since 1954 and disputes **Nepal's** territorial claims. The dispute reignited after **India** agreed with **China** to resume the pilgrimage, which was suspended in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

recent_articles.title: India rejects Nepal’s objection to Kailash Manasarovar Yatra via Lipulekh Pass - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** responded to **Nepal's** objection to the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra passing through Lipulekh Pass, stating that such territorial claims are "untenable." The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) clarified that Lipulekh Pass has been a long-standing route for the pilgrimage since 1954 and that India remains open to dialogue with **Nepal** on all bilateral issues.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: Kailash Mansarovar Yatra 2026: dates, routes, application process and all you need to know - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)** announced the schedule for this year's Kailash Manasarovar Yatra, which will take place between June and August.  A computer-generated, random selection process will be used to select 20 batches of 50 tourists each, with one batch traveling through Uttarakhand via Lipulekh Pass and another through Sikkim via Nathu La Pass.

recent_articles.title: Earth Day 2026: How Nature walks, parks, and trails are sparking a new conservation movement - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rohit Girotra**, co-founder of the Bangalore Butterfly Club (BBC), has seen a surge in interest in butterflies and butterfly-focused activities. The BBC, which began in 2012, now boasts nearly 600 members and offers guided walks at Doresanipalya Forest Research Station.  **Ashok Sengupta**, another BBC co-founder, believes that butterfly watching is an easy portal into the natural world for children. **Isaac Kehimkar**, a naturalist and photographer, has documented over 40 Facebook groups dedicated to butterflies worldwide. These groups have helped raise awareness of these insects through social media and mobile cameras. Butterfly parks and trails are also becoming increasingly popular across India, with locations like Sammilan Shetty's Butterfly Park in Karnataka offering educational programs on butterfly conservation.

recent_articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Government** celebrated National Panchayati Raj Day, highlighting the progress of women's reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).  While the Constitution mandates a 33% quota for women in urban and rural local bodies, 19 states have extended this provision to reserve 50% seats for women. However, data shows that the actual number of women representatives exceeds the prescribed quota in only 10 states/union territories, while four others fail to meet it.  The Ministry emphasized the increasing representation of women in PRIs, but acknowledged discrepancies between mandated and achieved quotas across various states.

recent_articles.title: Door-to-door visit by Census enumerators in eight States/U.T.s from April 16 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** announced the commencement of door-to-door enumeration for the first phase of the 2027 Population Census, known as the House Listing and Housing Operations (HLO). Beginning on April 16th in eight states and union territories including Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Goa, Karnataka, Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, and Delhi's NDMC area and Cantonment Board, enumerators will collect data for the HLO phase. This follows a 15-day self-enumeration period.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Census of springs: 63.4% of springs in Kerala are under private ownership - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Jal Shakti Ministry** released the first Spring Census Report, which revealed that 63.4% of springs in Kerala are under private ownership, significantly higher than other states like Karnataka and Tamil Nadu where public ownership dominates.  The report, covering Kerala, Karnataka, Ladakh, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, and Bihar, found that while Kerala has a high percentage of privately owned springs, the majority of springs across all surveyed states are publicly owned. The census, conducted by the **Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation**, aimed to inventory and map these critical water sources in response to depletion concerns.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 12 States and UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which saw a significant reduction in voter numbers across nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal with 83.86 lakh.  The revision identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters for removal. The consolidated electoral rolls across these regions saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.
